operations.description: Archive rows for the 16 spent config directories moved in this commit, plus this plan's own two configs. One row per group, each naming the commit that executed it and what it did.

edits.add_before:
| `ops-008-b3c1/*.json` … `ops-008-b3c7/*.json` (41 configs) | Spent — task 008 batch 3's seven merge clusters, executed 2026-08-24 in `775abd4`..`15075ac`, one cluster per plan and per commit. Nine agents removed, **29 → 21**; per-cluster detail lives in `plan-008-b3c1..b3c7-*.md` and the user-facing entry in `CHANGELOG.md`. **They sat in the live tree for a day because the gate that would have caught it scans nothing** — `test_queued_ops_configs_validate_against_head` enumerated top-level `.claude/plans/*.json` only, of which this repo has zero. 35 of these 41 already failed `validate-config-json.py`. Archived here as part of `plan-queued-ops-gate.md`, which widens the scan in the same commit. |
| `ops-b3c2-disclosure/`, `ops-b3c2-scan/` (2 configs) | Spent — executed with `15075ac`. Two batch-3 seam fixes, both of the same shape and both worth keeping visible: cluster 2 wrote its routing disclosure **in its own wording**, so the batch-wide grep for one canonical phrase did not see it; and the batch-wide consumer scan excluded its own file but not its sibling acceptance files, while cluster 7's closing table names all nine removed agents by design. Both are the `exact-string assertion misses a differently-punctuated copy` class. |
| `ops-b3c7-newline/ops.json` | Spent — executed with `cc7fb35`. W292, no newline at end of `tests/test_008_b3c7_harness_fold.py`. Mine, from cluster 7: the ops engine wrote the content exactly as given and the generated string had no trailing newline. Same family as the documented `add_before`/`add_after` newline trap. |
| `ops-findings-lane-a/`, `ops-findings-lane-b/` (2 configs) | Spent — executed with `24144f0`. Lane A hardened `knowledge-ledger.py`; lane B created `scripts/gen-plan-index.py`, `.claude/plans/INDEX.md` and `tests/test_plan_index.py` — the plan-lifecycle index and its `--check` drift gate. |
| `ops-findings-lane-a-r2/`, `ops-findings-lane-a-r2-tests/`, `ops-findings-lane-b-docs/`, `ops-findings-changelog/` (4 configs) | Spent — executed with `9c85238`. Round-2 review fixes for the ledger, with a regression test per path: the `--date` frontmatter-injection sink (a date carrying a newline and `---` terminated the block early, so an unverified entry read as `status: fixed, verified: true` and `prune --apply` archived the live finding at exit 0), and an unrecognised `status:` value failing open into `fixed`. Plus the `Plan-Id` trailer convention in `.ai/CHECKLISTS.md` and the CHANGELOG entries for both lanes. |
| `ops-queued-ops-gate/*.json` (2 configs) | Spent 2026-08-24, **`--no-approval` disclosed (Tier 2 but no security / schema / public-API surface: one test module plus these rows).** Fixes the gate that let every row above accumulate. `test_queued_ops_configs_validate_against_head` listed **top-level** `.claude/plans/*.json` only; every config in this repo lives in an `ops-<slug>/` subdirectory, so the scanned set was **empty** — 0 top-level, 50 in subdirectories, **35 already failing validation**. **Probed rather than reasoned about:** an invalid config at `.claude/plans/ops-PROBE/probe.json` leaves the test green, the byte-identical file at `.claude/plans/probe.json` turns it red. Now walks the tree, pruning `archive/` by name. The widening is proven by a second test that builds a throwaway plans tree (`ops-x/bad.json` plus `archive/ops-y/bad.json`) and asserts the helper returns the first and not the second — coverage that does not depend on the repo happening to contain a violation, which is the failure being fixed. Archive-first, widen-second, in one commit: widening first would have reddened the suite on 35 pre-existing failures, which is how a gate gets reverted instead of fixed. |
